source_landscape: Well documented (Wikipedia 'WannaCry ransomware attack', security retrospectives, and the 2026-09-05 canonical run): outbreak May 2017; EternalBlue exploit of SMBv1 patched in MS17-010 (March 2017); self-propagating worm behavior; roughly 150 countries affected; hardcoded kill-switch domain registration halted the spread.

expected_claims.statement: The WannaCry ransomware worm spread in May 2017 by exploiting EternalBlue, a Windows SMBv1 vulnerability patched by Microsoft in MS17-010.
expected_claims.note: Core mechanism; independently corroborated across sources.

expected_claims.statement: WannaCry affected computers in around 150 countries within days of its May 2017 outbreak.
expected_claims.note: Widely cited '150 countries' figure; magnitude claim.

expected_claims.statement: The rapid spread of WannaCry was halted after a researcher registered the worm's hardcoded kill-switch domain.
expected_claims.note: Kill-switch account; naming Marcus Hutchins optional.

expected_claims.statement: Systems that had installed the MS17-010 patch, released in March 2017, were not vulnerable to EternalBlue-based propagation.
